qwen.faq-2-answer: Qwen leads on multilingual coverage (119 languages) and math benchmarks. DeepSeek is cheaper at the API level. Llama has the largest ecosystem. The choice depends on your priority: global language support, raw cost savings, or community resources.
qwen.faq-3-question: What Qwen model sizes are available?
qwen.faq-3-answer: From 0.6B parameters (runs on edge devices) up to the Max variant (highest benchmarks). Mid-range sizes balance quality and compute cost for production. Everything is open-weight and self-hostable.
qwen.faq-4-question: Is Qwen suitable for production use outside China?
qwen.faq-4-answer: Yes. The open-weight license permits global commercial use. Self-host on any infrastructure worldwide, or access through providers like Setapp AI Gateway. When you self-host, your data never touches Alibaba's servers.
qwen.faq-5-question: Does Qwen support vision and code tasks?
qwen.faq-5-answer: Yes. Qwen-VL handles image understanding, OCR, and visual question answering. Qwen-Coder is tuned for programming tasks. Both carry the base model's multilingual strength, so you can work with visual or code content in any supported language.

copilot.hero-description: Microsoft Copilot brings AI directly into the apps you already use, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and VS Code. Instead of adding another tool to your workflow, Copilot helps you write, analyze, create, collaborate, and code right where you work.
copilot.card-description: Microsoft's AI assistant with deep Office integration. Powered by GPT with Bing web access built in.
copilot.gateway-title: How to use Copilot via Setapp AI Gateway
copilot.banner-title: Access Copilot-class models via Setapp AI Gateway
copilot.banner-body: Use the same GPT models powering Copilot — through one API, without Azure complexity.
copilot.best-1-body: Microsoft Copilot is built into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams. Draft documents, generate formulas, build presentations from outlines, summarize email threads, recap meetings — all without opening a separate app.
copilot.best-2-body: Copilot AI inherits Microsoft's full security stack: Azure AD, Conditional Access, DLP, and compliance boundaries. Data stays in your Microsoft 365 tenant. Copilot respects existing permissions — users only see what they're authorized to see.
copilot.best-3-body: Copilot for developers is the most adopted AI coding assistant, available in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, and Neovim. It suggests code as you type, understands your project context, and handles everything from autocomplete to multi-file edits and PR summaries.
copilot.use-1-body: Draft a Word doc from bullet points. Get Excel to write its own formulas. Build a PowerPoint from an outline. Summarize a 40-message Outlook thread. Copilot removes the formatting and drafting overhead that makes office work slow.
copilot.use-2-body: Copilot joins Teams meetings, captures notes and action items, and drafts follow-up emails. If you missed a meeting, it gives you a summary with key decisions and who's responsible for what.
copilot.use-3-body: GitHub Copilot suggests code as you type, writes tests, explains unfamiliar functions, and reviews PRs for bugs. For dev teams, it meaningfully reduces the time spent on boilerplate and routine code review.
copilot.use-4-body: Microsoft 365 Copilot can search across your organization's emails, documents, chats, and meeting recordings to answer questions. Instead of digging through SharePoint or old threads, you just ask.
copilot.faq-1-answer: An AI assistant built into Microsoft's product suite — Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams), Windows, Bing, and GitHub. It runs on OpenAI's GPT models combined with Microsoft Graph, so its answers are grounded in your organization's actual data.
copilot.faq-2-question: How does Copilot AI differ from ChatGPT?
copilot.faq-2-answer: ChatGPT is a standalone AI platform. Copilot is AI embedded inside the tools you already use. The key difference: Copilot has access to your documents, emails, calendar, and organizational context. ChatGPT is more versatile as a general assistant; Copilot is more immediately useful if you live in Microsoft 365.
copilot.faq-3-question: Copilot for developers — is GitHub Copilot worth it?
copilot.faq-3-answer: For most professional developers, yes. It noticeably reduces time on boilerplate, test writing, and documentation. Suggestions are context-aware to your project, and PR review catches real bugs. The ROI usually becomes clear within the first month of active use.
copilot.faq-4-answer: Microsoft 365 Copilot accesses data within your Microsoft 365 tenant — emails, docs, chats, meetings, calendars — but only what the authenticated user already has permission to view. It doesn't cross tenant boundaries or access personal accounts unless explicitly connected.
copilot.faq-5-question: Can I access Copilot's underlying models via API?
copilot.faq-5-answer: Microsoft offers Azure OpenAI Service for API access to the GPT models behind Copilot, with enterprise security and compliance. Through Setapp AI Gateway, you can also reach these models alongside Claude, Gemini, and others without dealing with Azure-specific setup.

perplexity.hero-description: Perplexity is an AI-powered search and research assistant that delivers direct answers with cited sources instead of a list of search results. It combines advanced language models with real-time web search to help you find, summarize, and verify information faster.
perplexity.card-description: Search-first AI with live web results and source citations in every response. Built for research and fact-checking.
perplexity.gateway-title: How to use Perplexity via Setapp AI Gateway
perplexity.banner-title: Add Perplexity Sonar to your stack via Setapp AI Gateway
perplexity.banner-body: Search-augmented AI answers with citations. One API call, sourced results, no retrieval pipeline to build.
perplexity.best-1-body: Perplexity AI retrieves information, synthesizes it, and shows you exactly where each claim came from. You can verify any part of any answer in seconds. That citation-first design makes it the most auditable AI tool for information retrieval.
perplexity.best-2-title: Real-time web retrieval with deep synthesis
perplexity.best-2-body: This isn't a static model guessing from training data. Perplexity search pulls live web results for every query, reads the sources, cross-checks them, resolves contradictions, and delivers a coherent answer. It's the difference between getting a link list and getting an actual answer.
perplexity.best-3-body: Perplexity routes each query to the best model for the job, including its own Sonar models built for search. Pro users can also tap GPT-5, Claude, and other frontier models as backends. You get the best retrieval infrastructure combined with whichever reasoning engine fits the question.
perplexity.use-1-body: Research a competitor, verify a claim, or explore a market trend and get cited sources with every answer. Perplexity compresses what used to be an hour of searching, opening tabs, and compiling notes into a single query.
perplexity.use-2-body: Find papers, understand technical concepts, and get up to speed on new fields with explanations grounded in actual published sources. Perplexity surfaces real research, not training-data approximations.
perplexity.use-3-body: Ask a technical question and get an answer that pulls from official docs, Stack Overflow, and GitHub — with links to each source. It's faster than manual doc-searching and more trustworthy than a standard LLM that might hallucinate API details.
perplexity.use-4-body: Get answers about breaking news, market shifts, product launches, or policy changes — all with source citations. The information is as current as the web itself because Perplexity fetches it live.
perplexity.faq-1-answer: Perplexity AI is an AI search engine that gives direct, sourced answers instead of traditional link lists. It combines large language models with real-time web retrieval, so it researches your question, reads the relevant sources, and presents a clear answer with citations.
perplexity.faq-2-question: How does Perplexity search differ from Google?
perplexity.faq-2-answer: Google gives you a list of websites to read yourself. Perplexity reads those sites for you, pulls the relevant information together, and delivers a synthesized answer with links to check.
perplexity.faq-3-question: Is Perplexity accurate? Can I trust the answers?
perplexity.faq-3-answer: Every factual claim is linked to a source, so you're not trusting the AI on faith — you're trusting cited references you can click and verify. That makes Perplexity more auditable than any standard chatbot. The citations are the trust mechanism.
perplexity.faq-4-answer: Sonar is the developer API for adding search-augmented AI to your own product. It combines web retrieval with language model reasoning and returns answers with citations that your app can display. Built for search, research, and information retrieval features.
perplexity.faq-5-question: Perplexity vs ChatGPT — which is better for research?
perplexity.faq-5-answer: For cited, verifiable research, Perplexity is clearly stronger. Every answer comes with checkable references. ChatGPT's Deep Research mode is capable but less consistently cited. For creative work, brainstorming, coding, or image generation, ChatGPT is the better tool. Use Perplexity to find and verify; use ChatGPT to create and build.
